sub: Ship design compliance checking · Meyer Turku challenge · Since AI Hackathon 2026
say: RuleTrace, with the RuleMate Copilot, checks ship designs against the regulations, shows exactly why something fails, and keeps engineers in control.
Load a design: a drawing, a 3D model, or a design file. Every part is coloured by its result, and nothing is accepted automatically.
Click a problem. This cabin door threshold is twenty-five millimetres, and the rule allows twelve point seven.
You see the requirement, the fix, and the exact rule text. Every comparison is done in code.
The engineer decides, and the decision is saved with name and time in an audit chain. Sign-off needs a second person.
Comparing two revisions shows what a change fixed, and what it broke.
Dashboards give the compliance lead a posture view, and the administrator the health of the system.
New rule sets are tested against the designs and today's rules before anyone relies on them.
The RuleMate Copilot opens beside the model. In confidential mode, nothing leaves this computer: a local model answers, and cloud services are off.
Answers come from the full regulation texts, including the Maritime Labour Convention. Every citation, number and quote is checked in code.
Other questions get a clearly labelled general answer. Its sources are checked, and an engineer approves it.
Check values compares a design with the limits, and a chart shows each value against its rule.

sub: Checked in code · traceable to a clause · approved by people · confidential by default
say: Checked in code, traceable to a clause, and approved by people. That is RuleTrace.
